solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Doctor had scrap for emergency shelter

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medic gives up some bits and pieces to make a refuge in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person but is a verb: HAD and SCRAP are shuffled to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A crash pad is somewhere to sleep at short notice, a makeshift place of refuge.

clue.text: Runs one sportsman finds more dangerous

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
the Roman numeral for one is I
a skier is one kind of sportsman

explanation.surface: A sportsman discovers that running is more hazardous than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Riskier is the comparative of risky, meaning carrying greater hazard.

clue.text: Perfume despatched, did you say?

indicators.note: a question about what was said tells us to listen to the word, not read it

parts.note: despatched means sent off

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether a bottle of fragrance has gone out in the post.
explanation.definitionFit: A scent is a pleasant smell, and by extension a bottled fragrance worn on the skin.

clue.text: Creature emerging occasionally in spring

indicators.note: only some letters of the word spring come out, every other one, starting from the second

explanation.surface: An animal pops out now and then in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A pig is a farm animal, one example of a creature.

clue.text: One protesting when residents moved

indicators.note: letters that are moved around are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone objects when the locals are relocated.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissenter disagrees with an established view, so is someone who objects or protests.

clue.text: Every fruit quietly disappearing

indicators.note: a thing that disappears is lost, so the letter for quietly is taken away

parts.note: a peach is a fruit
P stands for piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: Every bit of fruit is vanishing without a sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Each and every both refer to all members of a group taken one by one.

clue.text: Mountain sees First Lady taking breather

indicators.note: Eve takes on the rest that follows her, joining the two side by side

parts.note: Eve was the first woman, in the Bible
a breather is a short rest

explanation.surface: A climber sees the president's wife pausing for a breather on a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's wife; here it is Eve of Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the world's highest peak, in the Himalayas.

clue.text: Worry about daughter in revolutionary group

indicators.note: the word for worry sits round, about, the letter for daughter

parts.note: care is anxiety or worry

explanation.surface: A parent frets over a daughter who has joined a band of radicals.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadre is a small core of trained activists in a revolutionary party.

clue.text: Man perhaps insulted from time to time

indicators.note: only now and then is a letter of insulted used: every other one, from the first

explanation.surface: A man gets insulted every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man, between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, so Man is an example of one.

clue.text: Become calm in court?

definitions.meaning: couples who ... are courting, seeing each other regularly

explanation.surface: A defendant is urged to keep a level head before the judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks like a law court, but it is the verb for romancing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Going steady means keeping a regular romantic relationship, and also settling into a calm, even manner.

clue.text: Dislike Methodist as teacher to an extent

indicators.note: to an extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone dislikes a Methodist who works as a schoolteacher, at least partly.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is a feeling of aversion, a synonym of dislike as a noun.

clue.text: Resigns in stages, unhappy

parts.note: steps are stages in a process
feeling down means feeling unhappy

explanation.surface: Someone, miserable, quits their job gradually.
explanation.definitionFit: To step down is to leave a post or office voluntarily, an idiom for resigning.

clue.text: Paradise for PM once

definitions.meaning: the Garden of ... is the biblical paradise
Anthony ... was UK Prime Minister from 1955 to 1957

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister enjoys a blissful existence.
explanation.definitionFit: Eden was the garden of Genesis, a byword for an idyllic place; Anthony Eden held the UK premiership.

clue.text: Nothing much for pudding?

definitions.meaning: a layered dessert of sponge, custard and cream

explanation.surface: A modest dessert is offered as hardly worth mentioning.
explanation.definitionFit: Trifle means both a trivial thing and a classic British dessert of sponge, fruit, custard and cream.

clue.text: Force almost destroyed? That's rubbish

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for force in physics

indicators.note: something destroyed is broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A military force has been all but wiped out, which someone dismisses as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' looks like it trims a word, but it is the anagram fodder itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Flotsam is floating wreckage or debris, and figuratively worthless junk.

clue.text: Express disapproval of Egyptian king repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly says the king's short name is given again straight after itself

parts.note: Tut is short for Tutankhamun, the boy pharaoh

explanation.surface: Someone keeps tutting at an ancient Egyptian ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Tut-tut is the clicking sound people make, or say, to show mild annoyance or censure.

clue.text: Futile advice for a drug addict?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, ... is what you might tell an addict

explanation.surface: Telling an addict anything is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into two words of advice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something useless achieves nothing, the same as futile.

clue.text: Victor is a little treacherous

indicators.note: just a small part of treacherous is taken, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: A winner turns out to be slightly disloyal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' looks like a man's name but means a conqueror.
explanation.definitionFit: The victor of a struggle is often hailed as its hero, the champion who prevailed.

clue.text: Get rid of king? No difficulty about that

indicators.note: the word for no difficulty goes round, about, the letter for the king just named

parts.note: doing something with ease means with no difficulty
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether removing a monarch would be simple.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase something is to wipe it out, getting rid of it completely.

clue.text: Second person falling for cabaret performer

parts.note: someone who trips and falls is a tripper

explanation.surface: Somebody falls for a nightclub performer at first sight, or a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripper is a performer who undresses on stage, often in cabaret or club shows.

clue.text: Factory spy

definitions.meaning: an agent placed secretly inside an organisation

explanation.surface: An industrial works hides a secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant means a manufacturing site and also a mole planted to inform from within.

clue.text: What you might need to go beyond Dover?

parts.note: to pass something is to go beyond it
Dover is the English Channel port facing France

explanation.surface: A traveller wonders what document is needed to cross the Channel from Dover.
explanation.walkthrough: DOVER is the main English ferry port for France; leaving there for abroad needs this document.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the identity document a traveller must carry to cross international borders.

clue.text: Finest cannabis from the south

indicators.note: in a down answer, reading from the south means reading the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Premium-grade cannabis is brought up from southern regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Top quality means the best, so top can stand for finest.

clue.text: State of a reactionary priest

indicators.note: reactionary suggests going backwards, so the title for a priest is turned round

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a priest's title

explanation.surface: A conservative clergyman describes the condition of a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to declare or assert firmly, synonymous with the verb state.

clue.text: Group of policemen surrounding area to the west

indicators.note: in an across answer, heading west means reading right to left, backwards
the police word goes round the letter for area

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: A squad of officers encircles a district on its western side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' puts A inside MET to give MAET, which 'to the west' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A team is a set of people working together, a kind of group.

clue.text: Jobs for the boys — as postmen, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dodgy or unsound, so these letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: Someone suspects postal workers of handing posts to their mates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' is the anagram signal for POSTMEN plus I; 'as' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Jobs for the boys is a British idiom for favouring friends or relatives with appointments, which is favouritism of that kind.
